label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
narrative: Kirkpatrick is the single most consequential figure in the containment architecture. A laser and materials physicist (BS 1991, PhD 1995, University of Georgia), he came to AARO through the exact channels that would matter: the National Reconnaissance Office and CIA Directorate of Science and Technology 2003-2007, then the Defense Intelligence Agency 2007-2016 as Chief Technology Officer, Division Chief and Defense Intelligence Officer for Scientific and Technical Intelligence, then deputy director of intelligence roles at US Strategic Command and US Space Command, with a stint on the National Security Council 2017-2018 as Director of National Security Strategy. He was named the first director of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office when Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen Hicks established it by memorandum on 15 July 2022. He testified before the Senate Armed Services Emerging Threats and Capabilities Subcommittee on 19 April 2023 that AARO held over 650 cases and that spherical objects made up nearly half of them. He then became the public face of the Department's response to David Grusch: within days of the 26 July 2023 House Oversight hearing he posted on LinkedIn that the hearing was 'insulting' to the workforce, prompting the White House to publicly distance itself from him. He announced his departure on 7 November 2023 and left on 1 December 2023, and immediately took the job of Chief Technology Officer for Defense and Intelligence Programs at Oak Ridge National Laboratory - a laboratory operated by UT-Battelle that had supported AARO during his tenure, and which in 2024 was given custody of the alleged UAP material sample AARO analysed. On 19 January 2024 he published an op-ed in Scientific American arguing the whole disclosure record was 'a textbook example of circular reporting' traceable to 'a small group of interconnected believers' seeded by Robert Bigelow and AATIP. He shaped, then supervised the rollout of, the Historical Record Report Volume I, released 8 March 2024 after he had already left. In September 2025 he told the New York Post that Rep. Anna Paulina Luna's oversight was 'playhouse politics' and that the congressional UAP hearings were 'a disgrace' and 'reality TV'; Luna's office called him 'a known documented liar' who 'blocked the release of information' and 'tried to discredit witnesses.' By May 2026 his own successor, Jon Kosloski, had - per Luna - apologised to members of Congress for the conduct of the prior AARO leadership.
